item.title: Water Cycle With Exact Labels

turns.text: Make a 10-second widescreen water-cycle explainer with a friendly voice-over you write. Show water rising, clouds forming, then rain. Label those stages exactly “Evaporation”, “Condensation”, and “Precipitation”, in that order. No other on-screen text.

item.tests: Tests exact rendered labels, correct stage mapping, and coordinated original narration in a short explainer.

answer_sheet.Exact on-screen labels: Evaporation; Condensation; Precipitation. Use that capitalization and order, without quotation marks.
answer_sheet.Other text: No other on-screen text, including subtitles.
answer_sheet.Voice and language: Friendly English voice; specific voice is your call.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second widescreen video has a friendly, intelligible English voice-over explaining the depicted cycle.
Water rises as vapor, clouds form, and rain falls, in that order.
The visible labels read exactly 'Evaporation', 'Condensation', and 'Precipitation', with no misspellings.
Each label is legible and appears with its corresponding stage, in the requested order.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: Create a 10-second 16:9 educational water-cycle explainer with synchronized English voice-over. Clean colorful 2D science animation, fixed wide composition of a lake, green land, sky and warm sun. Three sequential stages with smooth transitions: 0–3.3 seconds show water vapor rising from the sun-warmed lake with upward flowing wisps; display exactly the single label “Evaporation”. 3.3–6.6 seconds show vapor cooling and gathering into fluffy clouds; replace the previous label with exactly “Condensation”. 6.6–10 seconds show raindrops falling from the clouds to the land and lake; replace previous label with exactly “Precipitation”. These three exact English labels must appear in that order, one at a time, large, high contrast and correctly spelled. NO other on-screen text at all: no title, no subtitles, no captions, no credits, no additional words. Friendly clear narrator speaks this exact script naturally within ten seconds, aligned with stages: “Sunlight warms water into vapor. It cools into clouds. Then water falls as rain, continuing the cycle.” Prioritize intelligible voice-over, accurate stage ordering, clear motion and exact labels. No music needed.
